activity_context.topic_title: The Matrix of a Linear Transformation Relative to a Basis

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Transformation Given the Images of the Basis Vectors
examples.problem:
Let $\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2,\mathbf{b}_3 \}$ be a basis of $\mathbb{R}^3.$ The matrix $[\,\mathbf{T}\,]_{\mathcal{B}}$ of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^3 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066994/assets/e07cc9382ff64be2d3ad03974dee5e61f814457f06dbe4e755a72e69efc7608c.png)

Find the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & ={b}_{1}+{b}_{3}, \\ T({b}_{2}) & ={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}, \\ T({b}_{3}) & ={b}_{2}+{b}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we write down the coordinates of the images relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066994/assets/9b7de12d5e69074e64281b8060088e458c04007ed48f7640e85619898f96dad7.png)

Now, the $\mathcal{B}$-matrix for $\mathbf{T}$ is a matrix  whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1),$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2),$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}.$ Therefore, we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066994/assets/2dd5d507303f356fcd3632c8dade2e8a656169de1118b4443bd651cca45d6660.png)

Finally, $a=1,$ $b=1,$ $c=0$ and 

$$
a+b+c = 1+1+0 = 2.
$$

feedback.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[T(x)]_{B}$, given that
$\,$ $[T]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 11 & -4\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
The image of $[x]_{B}$ relative to the basis $B$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{B} & =[T]_{B}[x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 11 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
